title: He Fought WWII With a Bow and a Sword 🏹 #shorts
cast: a wild-eyed British officer with a big moustache, steel helmet, carrying a longbow and a Scottish broadsword, playing bagpipes

lines.say: In World War Two, while everyone carried guns, one officer went into battle with a bow and a sword.
shots: {hero} charging forward with a longbow on a misty battlefield
close-up of {hero} with a wild grin under his helmet

lines.say: His name was Jack Churchill. His men called him Mad Jack.
shots: {hero} standing in front of a group of soldiers, arms crossed
soldiers whispering and laughing in a trench

lines.say: He was a champion archer, and he played the bagpipes.
shots: {hero} aiming a longbow at a target in a green field
{hero} playing bagpipes on a hill at sunrise

lines.say: In France, in 1940, he shot an enemy soldier with an arrow. It's thought to be the last bow kill of the war.
shots: an arrow flying across a foggy French village
{hero} hiding behind a stone wall with his bow

lines.say: He led commando raids with a Scottish broadsword at his side.
shots: {hero} leaping off a landing boat onto a rocky beach with a sword
commandos running up a beach at dawn

lines.say: He was captured, and escaped from a prison camp.
shots: {hero} crawling under barbed wire at night
{hero} walking along a railway line at dawn, free

lines.say: He later said that any officer who went into action without his sword was improperly dressed.
shots: {hero} straightening his uniform with his sword in front of a mirror

lines.say: A real person, not a movie character. Would you follow him into battle?
shots: {hero} silhouetted against a sunset with bow and sword
a longbow and sword resting against a wooden chair

description:
British officer 'Mad Jack' Churchill carried a longbow, a broadsword and bagpipes in WWII, is credited with one of the last recorded bow kills in war (1940), and escaped from captivity. A true story.

Sources: National Army Museum; Wikipedia: Jack Churchill.

Made with AI-assisted pictures and voice.
